description: Saskatoon Transit will monitor zero-emission bus technology.
It will explore small-scale zero-emission bus pilots.
City requests exemptions for zero-emission buses beyond 2028.
The plan informs future fleet renewal and climate action.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
CUTRIC CEO explained heavy-duty electric bus maintenance is complex, unlike light-duty vehicles.
Bus riders and Saskatoon Climate Hub spoke on the zero-emission bus plan.
Public speakers strongly opposed the report's recommendation to delay electric bus procurement.
Zero-emission buses offer benefits like reduced pollution for vulnerable communities.
Zero-emission buses reduce tailpipe emissions and improve air quality.
CUTRIC will host a free public webinar to explain the report's methodology.

speakers.name: Robert Clipperton
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Bus Riders of Saskatoon
said: Opposes report's reversal to no electric bus procurement.
CUTRIC report lacks utility by not considering a mixed fleet.
Advocates deploying up to 40 electric buses to avoid costly upgrades.

speakers.name: Caylin Lee
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Zero Emission Bus Full Fleet Implementation Plan
said: CUTRIC report is flawed, contradicting previous SRC findings.
Report lacks transparency, not showing data or assumptions.
Contains obvious errors, like ludicrous part replacement cost estimates.

speakers.name: Jory Vermette
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Zero Emission Bus Implementation Plan
said: Report focuses purely on fiscal matters, ignoring critical factors.
Zero-emission buses offer environmental, health, and social equity benefits.
Urges council to reject the report and adopt a climate-focused strategy.

description: Maintains Tier 2 energy efficiency standards for new home construction.
Aims to reduce long-term utility costs for homeowners.

chips.text: Approved (8-3)
8 for, 3 against
Mayor Block stated cost recovery for homeowners from these standards is less than five years.
Builders operating in Warman, Martensville, and Corman Park face differing energy standards.
City decision to maintain higher local energy standards is an unprecedented situation.
Saskatoon & Region Home Builders' Association presented industry concerns on costs and delays.
Councillor Donauer argued for aligning with provincial Tier 1 to support housing affordability.
The decision aligns with the city's low emissions community plan.
Administration will monitor impacts and report back to Council next year.

speakers.name: Nicole Burgess
speakers.organization: Saskatoon and Region Home Builders Association
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Energy Regulation Opts for Building Stands_Red
said: Many Saskatoon builders voluntarily met Tier 2 standards before regulation.
Regulatory delays and inconsistencies add significant costs for home buyers.
Builders need certainty, collaboration, and a level playing field.
